title: Semantic Audit Verdict
description: A structured, machine-readable verdict from the semantic audit layer (ARCHITECTURE.md §5). This layer is heuristic, not sound: it checks correspondence between a kernel-accepted statement and its stated intent, not a fact with an independent re-derivation procedure (ARCHITECTURE.md §7). failure_reason is null iff verdict == 'pass' (INTERFACES.md property 3: null never means a guess, it is the explicit encoding of 'no failure'). Version history: 1.0.0 is the original format; 1.1.0 adds the 'unexercised-hypothesis' failure reason (an enumerating checker found no explored state that VIOLATED an obligation's precondition, so the implication was never exercised) and changes nothing else. Adding a value to a closed enum is a change a consumer must be able to notice, so it travels with a version bump (INTERFACES.md property 5); 1.0.0 documents remain valid and may not carry the 1.1.0-only reason.

schema_version.description: The format version this document was written to. Both accepted versions validate; the allOf block below forbids a 1.0.0 document from carrying a failure reason introduced in 1.1.0.

failure_reason.description: Nullable. Null iff verdict == 'pass'. A specific, machine-readable code — never free text — when verdict == 'fail'.

details.description: Structured evidence for the verdict (which check ran, what it found). Never a free-text narrative — a caller should be able to branch on its fields, not grep it.

produced_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when this verdict was produced.

failure_reason.description: A 1.0.0 document predates the 'unexercised-hypothesis' reason and may not use it.
